identity.name: Sodium ascorbate
identity.chemical_class: Sodium salt of L-ascorbic acid (vitamin C derivative)

function.mechanism: Acts as a reducing antioxidant that limits oxidation and, in nitrite-cured systems, can lower residual nitrite and influence nitrosamine formation.
common_food_categories: other foods using antioxidant preservatives under GMP

adi.basis: EFSA 2015 re-evaluation concluded no need for a numerical ADI for ascorbic acid and its salts

efsa.key_finding: No safety concern at reported uses and use levels for ascorbic acid (E300), sodium ascorbate (E301), and calcium ascorbate (E302).

fda.notes: GRAS when used in accordance with good manufacturing practice (and good feeding practice for animal feed).

adi.basis: ADI not specified (group ADI for ascorbic acid and its sodium, potassium, and calcium salts)

concerns.summary: A 2026 prospective cohort (NutriNet-Sante) reported an association between sodium ascorbate exposure and higher type 2 diabetes incidence among preservative additives; causality is not established.
Food-system studies show nitrosamine outcomes are process/formulation dependent, although sodium ascorbate generally lowers residual nitrite.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2015 reported no genotoxicity concern and no safety concern at reported uses/use levels.
In a rat bladder carcinogenesis promotion model, sodium ascorbate did not increase papillomas or transitional cell carcinomas (PMID:29471778).
JECFA and EFSA both use non-numerical ADI conclusions (ADI not specified / no numerical ADI needed) for this substance group.

adi_exceedance.notes: Numeric ADI exceedance assessment is not applicable because EFSA/JECFA do not set a numerical ADI for this additive group.

risk_assessment.rationale: Core regulatory evaluations (EFSA, JECFA, FDA GRAS) are broadly reassuring, but an emerging observational epidemiology signal supports caution rather than a fully risk-free label.
key_factors: EFSA 2015: no safety concern at reported uses; no numerical ADI needed
JECFA: ADI not specified (group ADI context)
FDA eCFR GRAS listings under GMP
No IARC classification identified for sodium ascorbate
Recent observational association with type 2 diabetes requires follow-up
